Add a play

⚠ Automatic parsing is a best guess, not a promise. Unusual formatting can merge speeches, miss speakers, or turn dialogue into stage directions — usually without an error message. After adding a play, open Full Script beside your original and spot-check several speeches, especially scene starts and endings, before you rehearse from it. If your script uses odd conventions (lowercase speaker names, prose editions, messy PDF copy-paste), don’t fight the parser: the kit’s PLAY_CONVERSION_GUIDE.md lets an AI assistant convert it properly — and tells you how to verify the result. Never trust an unverified script the night before a performance.
Script format help 
Everything before the first scene heading = title page.
ACT 1, SCENE 1        starts a scene (also: PROLOGUE, SCENE 2)
[A castle]            lines in [brackets] are stage directions
HAMLET 1.1.1          ALL-CAPS line = speaker (number optional)
HAMLET [aside]        inline directions on the speaker line work
To be or not to be. | a gloss     " | " adds a side-note (optional)
HORATIO: One-line speeches work like this too.
INDEX                 optional back-matter section

Files: .txt in this format, a play.json from the builder kit,
or a play bundle exported from this app (play + your notes).
ALWAYS spot-check a newly added play against your source —
the parser guides, you verify.
Full text of the Hundsness edition (Second Quarto, 1599), parsed from your uploaded PDF; editorial glosses preserved.
App · ⚡ marks a shared verse line: the half-line completes the previous speaker's — pick up the cue with no pause.
